info.title: WorkCam Verification Service
info.description: Prototype verification service for WorkCam trusted photography. This is NOT a production-grade authentication service.

post.description:
Register a public key with a device_id.

SECURITY: This endpoint is for DEVELOPMENT/TESTING ONLY.
- Requires explicit allow_test_registration=true parameter
- In production, this endpoint must be DISABLED
- Production will use App Attest formal registration flow
- Does NOT allow overwriting existing registrations
- Returns error if device_id conflicts with existing registration

Store a record for replay detection.

SECURITY: This endpoint enforces strict validation:
- photo_base64 is MANDATORY (cannot be None or empty)
- Signature must be mathematically valid
- Public key must be registered
- Device identity must be consistent
- Photo hash MUST match the manifest's photo_hash

Invalid evidence will NOT occupy the record_id.

Zero-byte photos are supported if explicitly provided and hash matches,
but must be distinguished from missing photos.

This is a development/testing endpoint, NOT a production-grade
trusted registration service.

get.description:
Check if a record exists in the store.
This is a development/testing endpoint.

post.description:
Create a time anchor for a batch of offline records.

EXPERIMENTAL: This endpoint is for research only.

The server will:
1. Record the current time
2. Generate a random challenge
3. Sign the anchor data
4. Return the signed receipt

IMPORTANT: The server time proves the records existed BEFORE this time,
but does NOT prove when they were actually created.

Returns:
    TimeAnchorResponse with signed receipt

Raises:
    HTTPException: If validation fails (400), conflict (409), or persistence error (500)

Verify a time anchor receipt.

EXPERIMENTAL: This endpoint is for research only.

Checks:
1. key_id is registered (reject unknown keys)
2. Signature is valid using the correct public key
3. verification_status matches signed value (prevent elevation)
4. All signed fields match stored values
5. Receipt exists in server storage (requires server)

Args:
    receipt: The receipt to verify
    check_storage: If True, also check against server storage.
                  If False, only verify signature offline.

Returns:
    TimeAnchorVerification with trust level analysis

get.description:
Get the server's public key for verifying anchor signatures.

EXPERIMENTAL: This endpoint is for research only.

Returns:
    Public key in PEM format with key_id

Get an anchor receipt by anchor_id.

EXPERIMENTAL: This endpoint is for research only.

Returns:
    TimeAnchorReceipt if found

Raises:
    HTTPException: If anchor not found
Health check for time anchor service.

post.description:
P2 identity flow step 1: server issues a single-use nonce for the
enrolled device. The device then signs the nonce with its P-256 key
(the SAME key as evidence signing - one identity).

P2 identity flow step 2: {device_token, nonce, signature_b64} ->
verifies the nonce signature with the ENROLLED public key. Private
keys never leave the device. W013: routes through the SQLite-backed
challenge store (device_identity.verify_challenge_signature).

get.description:
Stream the assembled file back (byte-level verification for the
client). Only available after COMPLETE; production-disabled like
every other route here.

post.description:
Move photos to an AUTHORIZED project (caller-owned + active).

WHOLE-BATCH PRE-VALIDATION (task constraint): every photo and the
target project are checked BEFORE any row is written; any violation
rejects the entire batch with a typed error and per-photo details -
a rejected move never leaves a half-moved set. After pre-validation
the per-photo ledger flow takes over (idempotent replays, retryable
failures).

Guard rails (evidence discipline):
  - photos linked to an inspection issue are NOT movable (moving
    would strand a cross-project before/after association, which
    the W013 single-link path forbids)
  - photos sitting in an ARCHIVED project are NOT movable
    (archived = frozen work product)
  - moving to the photo's current project is an idempotent no-op
  - only mvp_photos.project_id changes - evidence links, originals
    bindings, annotations and their verification state are untouched

Render the SAME watermark template+fields over a set of photos.

Reuses the W011 render path (render_watermark_for_photo): the
original bytes are read-only, the server resolves each photo's
evidence status itself, and per-photo idempotency is the W011
(photo, template, params-hash, original-sha) key - re-running an
already-rendered photo returns the SAME derivative.

Executions happen OUTSIDE the ledger transaction (rendering is
CPU-heavy; the W011 engine manages its own transactions). The
ledger row is written after a successful render, so an interrupted
batch replays stored receipts and re-renders only the missing ones
(the W011 idempotency probe makes even a double render harmless).

Build an export package (ZIP: manifest.json + originals by
content hash + guide) and register it for download.

Per-photo resume semantics: a photo's manifest ENTRY is the batch
ledger's stored result. Retrying the failed subset under the same
batch_id re-uses the stored entries (no re-execution) and builds a
NEW export containing every photo - the client ends up with one
complete package. Duplicate content is stored ONCE (content-addressed
originals/{sha256}.jpg), mirroring the duplicate-detection view.
The export NEVER contains tokens, enrollment codes or key material.

get.description:
Stored receipts for one batch (the resume view). Only
SUCCEEDED/replayed photos live in the ledger; a photo absent here
was either never processed or failed - both stay retryable under
the same batch_id.

Business-metadata view for one photo: tags, category, note.
Deliberately SEPARATE from the photo/evidence representation - the
evidence view (GET /photos/{id}) never mixes these in.

Filter + search across ALL of the caller's photos with a STABLE
keyset pagination.

Stability (task requirement): the page key is (sort_value,
photo_id) - a total order on the result set. New rows inserted
between page pulls can never shift already-returned rows: they
either sort before the current cursor (already passed - the client
sees them on the NEXT query) or after (normal forward flow). No
offset is used, so there is no skip/duplicate window at all.

Filters compose with AND. `q` matches the original filename, the
business note or any tag (case-insensitive substring, LIKE
metacharacters escaped). captured_from/to compare the
client-claimed captured_at lexically (ISO-8601) - sorting by it is
allowed, trusting it is not.

Content-addressed duplicate detection: photos are grouped by
their original_sha256 (SHA-256 IS the identity, W007 rule) across
ALL of the caller's projects. Duplicates are REPORTED, never
deleted - originals are immutable evidence and deletion is a human
decision outside this API.

Group-level keyset pagination keyed on original_sha256.

post.description:
Server-side verification of a registered evidence link.

The client submits the verification MATERIAL (manifest / anchor
receipt); the server runs the EXISTING trusted verification paths
(W002 signature service, W003 anchor service - unmodified) and
writes the resulting status back. Clients still cannot submit a
status: the computed value is the only thing that lands in the DB.

Traceability + binding guards (fail fast, 400 - no state change):
  - signature_manifest: manifest.record_id MUST equal the link's
    evidence_reference, and manifest.photo_hash MUST equal the
    photo's original_sha256 (anti cross-photo misbinding)
  - time_anchor: receipt.batch_id MUST equal the evidence_reference

put.description:
Store the ORIGINAL bytes for an owned photo record and bind it.

The body is the raw photo bytes. Integrity is verified DURING the
write (hash-while-streaming): a mismatch with the photo's REGISTERED
original_sha256 rejects the request and persists NOTHING.

Idempotent: same photo + same content -> same binding; a photo may
be re-uploaded with identical bytes freely.
Immutable: different content for an ALREADY-BOUND photo is 409
(the photo's registered hash defines the object; changing it is
evidence tampering, not an update).

get.description:
Authorized download of the ORIGINAL bytes. Ownership chains
through the photo's project (cross-subject -> 404 identical to
not-found). No disk path is ever exposed - the object is addressed
by the photo's registered hash and read from the content-addressed
store.

Storage integrity + the photo's evidence chain, in one view:

  storage says: do the bytes exist and match the hash
  evidence says: has the server verified anything about origin

These are SEPARATE claims (P0 requirement) - a stored, intact object
is 'file integrity verified', never 'authentic photo'.

post.description:
Submit an offline-queued batch of operations.

Each operation executes IN ORDER and gets an individual receipt
(partial success); idempotent replays return the STORED receipt
without re-execution. Authentication and ownership apply to the
CALLER on every operation - replaying someone's captured batch with
your own token cannot touch their resources (their owner_token is
not in the payload; ownership is resolved server-side).

get.description:
Incremental pull for the caller's OWN events only.

The cursor is the last seq the client has seen. Restart-stable:
seq is AUTOINCREMENT in the business DB. Pagination correctness
under concurrent inserts: the page query filters seq > cursor and
seq <= cursor + page_high_water (captured BEFORE reading), so rows
inserted mid-pull appear in the NEXT page, never cause a skip or
duplicate.

post.description:
Prove-of-possession flow (W005 semantics, DB-backed nonce):
issue a single-use nonce for the enrolled device to sign.

{device_token, nonce, signature_b64} -> verifies with the
ENROLLED public key. Private keys never leave the device.

Issue the single-use nonce the CURRENT key must sign before the
device may swap in a new key. Caller = the enrolled device itself.

Swap the enrolled key after an OLD-key possession proof. The
token stays; the key changes; the old key goes to history.

Evidence-verifier interface: registration state of a public key
WITHOUT any signature-math claim (math and registration are two
different verification questions - never conflate them).

ZIP delivery package: report.pdf + originals/ + derivatives/ +
manifest.json + verification-guide.txt. Options control inclusion.
Sensitive material (tokens, enrollment codes, keys) is NEVER
exported. Returns the ZIP inline (bytes) with a manifest header.

Manually link a photo to an issue by role. The comparison is a
HUMAN association - the API response says so.

Generate a before/after side-by-side derivative. Reads the two
originals (never modifies them), draws each with its label, and
returns the composed JPEG.

put.description:
Store the original bytes WITHOUT buffering the whole body in
memory (the legacy `await request.body()` path must hold the full
file; this endpoint hashes and writes chunk-by-chunk, so a 500 MB
photo costs ~256 KB of heap instead of 500 MB).

Semantics identical to the legacy PUT: claimed hash from the
photo's registered original_sha256, mismatch -> 400 + nothing
persisted, idempotent replay on identical bytes, never overwrites
an existing object.

get.description:
Get-or-generate this photo's thumbnail. Content-addressed by the
ORIGINAL's hash: photos sharing the same original share one cache
file (free dedup). The original is opened read-only.

EvidenceStatus.title: EvidenceStatus
EvidenceStatus.description:
Evidence trust levels (from highest to lowest):

FULLY_ATTESTED: All checks passed including device attestation and time anchor.
                This is the highest trust level, rarely achieved in practice.

CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY_VALID: Signature math valid, photo hash matches, key registered.
                        BUT device attestation is unknown/unverified.
                        This does NOT prove the device is genuine.

SIGNATURE_VALID: Signature math valid, but photo not verified or key not registered.

PARTIAL: Some checks passed, some incomplete.

UNVERIFIED: Checks could not be performed.

INVALID: One or more checks failed.

remediation_note.title: Remediation Note
remediation_note.description: HUMAN-entered remediation recommendation; rendered as MANUAL INPUT in reports

LidarMeasurementRef.title: LidarMeasurementRef
LidarMeasurementRef.description:
Reference to a B02-W016 LiDAR analyzer record. The report only
cites the record id and its device-data status - it never renders a
measurement value as verified or certified.

TimeAnchorReceipt.title: TimeAnchorReceipt
TimeAnchorReceipt.description:
Receipt stored by client for later verification.

Contains all information needed to verify the anchor later.

SIGNED FIELDS (can be verified offline with server public key):
- anchor_id, key_id, batch_id, server_received_at, challenge
- chain_head_hash, chain_tail_hash, record_count

UNSIGNED FIELDS (cannot be verified offline):
- device_reported_start_time, device_reported_end_time
- verification_status, stored_at

TimeAnchorRequest.title: TimeAnchorRequest
TimeAnchorRequest.description:
Client request to anchor a batch of offline records.

The client submits:
- batch_id: Unique identifier for this batch
- chain_head_hash: Hash of the first record in the chain
- chain_tail_hash: Hash of the last record in the chain
- record_count: Number of records in the batch
- device_reported_start_time: Device's claim of when first record was created
- device_reported_end_time: Device's claim of when last record was created

IMPORTANT: Submitting only hashes means the server can only provide
DIGEST_ANCHORED status. For CHAIN_VERIFIED or PHOTO_VERIFIED, the
client must submit actual records/photos.

TimeAnchorResponse.title: TimeAnchorResponse
TimeAnchorResponse.description:
Server response after anchoring a batch.

The server provides:
- anchor_id: Unique identifier for this anchor
- key_id: Identifier for the signing key (for key rotation)
- server_received_at: Server's timestamp of when batch was received
- challenge: Random value to prevent replay attacks
- server_signature: Signature over the anchor data
- verification_status: What the server actually verified

SIGNED FIELDS (included in signature):
- anchor_id, batch_id, server_received_at, challenge
- chain_head_hash, chain_tail_hash, record_count

UNSIGNED FIELDS (not included in signature):
- device_reported_start_time, device_reported_end_time
- verification_status

IMPORTANT: server_received_at proves the digest existed BEFORE this time,
but does NOT prove when the actual photos were taken.

TimeAnchorVerification.title: TimeAnchorVerification
TimeAnchorVerification.description:
Result of verifying a time anchor receipt.

This distinguishes between:
1. Signature verification (can be done offline with public key)
2. Storage verification (requires checking server records)

VerificationStatus.title: VerificationStatus
VerificationStatus.description:
What the server actually verified vs what it only signed.

IMPORTANT: The server signature only proves it received and signed
the submitted digest. It does NOT prove the server verified the
actual content unless explicitly stated.

DIGEST_ANCHORED: Server signed the submitted digest (hashes, count, times).
                 This is the MINIMUM guarantee. The server did NOT verify
                 the actual records, photos, or chain integrity.

CHAIN_VERIFIED: Server actually verified the complete record chain.
                This requires the client to submit all records, not just
                the head/tail hashes.

PHOTO_VERIFIED: Server actually verified photo content matches hashes.
                This requires the client to submit actual photos.

RECORD_COUNT_VERIFIED: Server actually counted and verified each record.
                       This requires the client to submit all records.

WatermarkFields.title: WatermarkFields
WatermarkFields.description:
Every field independently togglable (show_* flag per field). The
value objects carry their OWN trust metadata so the renderer can
label honestly without guessing.

app__models__capture__TimeTrustLevel.title: TimeTrustLevel
app__models__capture__TimeTrustLevel.description:
How much we trust the timestamp:

SERVER_ANCHORED: Server verified the time when record was submitted.
DEVICE_REPORTED: Only device-reported time, no server verification.
UNKNOWN: No time information available.

app__models__time_anchor__TimeTrustLevel.title: TimeTrustLevel
app__models__time_anchor__TimeTrustLevel.description:
Classification of time evidence trustworthiness.

SERVER_ANCHORED: Server recorded receipt time. Proves records existed
                 before this time, but not when they were created.

DEVICE_REPORTED: Only device-reported time. Cannot be trusted as
                 accurate without server corroboration.

UNVERIFIED: No time evidence available.

deviceToken.name: X-Device-Token
deviceToken.description: Random opaque token issued by /api/v1/devices/enroll (enrollment code required). The caller's ownership key.

adminCode.name: X-Admin-Code
adminCode.description: The out-of-band enrollment code doubles as the MVP admin secret (known RBAC gap).
